# Independent review of the least measure in the group generated by two Chebyshev units

<a id="finding"></a>
## The minimum and its uniform expansion

At 2026-11-24T17:36 an agent outside the proof development independently reviewed for Yin the complete [minimum theorem](../../claims/Yin_C_G0902_v1.md#minimum) in the proof dated 2026-11-24T17:35.
The reviewer received the fixed proof and assignment, consulted the cited endpoint construction, and received no development dialogue, author explanation or previous finding on this theorem.
The proof establishes the stated minimum, its two attaining exponent pairs, the assertion with an optional torsion factor and the uniform asymptotic formula.

The leading coefficients of \(H\) are \(1,4,2M\) even when \(n=4\), since \(C_d\) is monic of degree \(n-3\).
Its constant coefficient is twice an odd integer and every intermediate coefficient is even.
At the \(d+1\) specified angles the numerator of the sine quotient for \(C_d\) alternates between \(1\) and \(-1\), including at \(\theta=\pi\) by continuity.
The strict sign comparison still holds when \(4^{n-1}=2M\), because \(\lvert Mx-1\rvert=M\lvert x\rvert+1\) at every sample.
The resulting \(d\) negative roots and the positive root leave two places, both occupied by the nonreal pair since the sum of squares is negative.
The negative real embedding makes the quadratic discriminant nonsquare, so all \(2n\) reciprocal lifts occur as conjugates.
The sum and sum of squares of the traces give \(A=O(n)\), \(B^2=2M+O(n^2)\) for the nonreal trace \(A+iB\).
For its exterior lift \(re^{i\psi}\), the identity \(\lvert 2+A+iB\rvert^2=r^2+r^{-2}+2\cos(2\psi)\) gives \(r^2=2M+O(n^2)\).
The three exterior lifts have moduli \(T,r,r\).
The bounds \(C_d(w)\ge 2d+1\) and \(w<M^{-1}\) give \(1-Mw=O(M^{1-n})\) with an absolute constant, so \(\log T=M^{-1/2}+O(M^{-3/2})\).
Adding \(2\log r\) yields the claimed expansion uniformly, since \(n=O(\log M)\).

The product \((p-qT)(pT-q)/T=1-Mw\) gives the asserted formula for \(Y+Y^{-1}-2\).
The product of all conjugates of \(1-Mw\) is \(M^n H(1/M)=1+4M=L^2\), which gives integrality of \(Y+Y^{-1}\) and hence of both \(Y\) and \(Y^{-1}\).
At the positive place \(Y>1\) and \(Y\ge Y+Y^{-1}-2=L^2w/(1-Mw)\), giving the stated lower bound on \(\log Y\).
At the nonreal place \(\lvert p-q\zeta\rvert\ge qr-p\), so the displayed identity for \(Y_\zeta+p/q\) yields \(\log\lvert Y_\zeta\rvert=O(M^{-1/2})\).
The involution of the quadratic lift supplies opposite logarithms at each place.
Restricting to the field generated by any product preserves a conjugate realizing the nonnegative logarithm from the pair, even if several embeddings restrict to the same one.
Extending either embedding across a root of unity preserves that modulus.
For \(b\ne0\) and \(\lvert a\rvert\ge3\lvert b\rvert\), the nonreal place contributes at least \(\lvert b\rvert(3\log r-\lvert\log\lvert Y_\zeta\rvert\rvert)\), which exceeds \(\log T+2\log r\) uniformly for large \(q\).
For \(\lvert a\rvert<3\lvert b\rvert\), the positive place contributes at least \(\lvert b\rvert((n-1)\log M-O(1)-3\log T)\), again strictly larger since \(n\ge4\).

For every nonzero integer \(a\), fixing \(T^a\) forces the image of \(T\) to have modulus \(T\).
The complete list of conjugates and \(1<T<r\) leave exactly one such image, so separability gives \(\mathbb Q(T^a)=\mathbb Q(T)\).
The measure therefore scales by \(\lvert a\rvert\), including negative powers by reciprocity.
If \(\omega\) has order \(k\), powering \(\omega T^a\) to exponent \(k\) multiplies absolute height by \(k\) and can only lower the degree.
This gives \(m(\omega T^a)\ge m(T^{ak})/k=\lvert a\rvert m(T)\).
Taking \(\omega=1\) attains the bound at \(a=\pm1\), and the expansion gives divergence while \(T\to1\).
